report.title: Search filter persists after clicking Shortcuts even when search box is empty
report.body:
### Pre-submission Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and this bug has not been reported yet
- [x] I have tested this issue on the [demo site](https://demo.usememos.com) or the latest version

### Where did you encounter this bug?

Latest stable version (self-hosted)

### Memos Version

v0.25.3

### Bug Description

This issue can confuse users because after selecting a Shortcut, one would normally expect the previous search criteria to reset if the search input is empty. However, the old filter still influences results, creating misleading or unintended results.

### Steps to Reproduce


1. Go to the Memos application and perform a search using a keyword in the search box.
2. Click on one of the Shortcuts items.
3. Although the search box becomes empty after selecting the shortcut, the previous search filter still remains active, affecting the results displayed.

### Expected Behavior

After clicking a Shortcut, the old keyword search filter should be cleared if the search box is empty, and only the shortcut filter should take effect.

### Screenshots & Additional Context

_No response_

a memo containing the word 'banana' exists
a shortcut that matches memos containing 'banana' exists

Do each step once, in order. If the app behaves unexpectedly, do not undo, retry, repair or work around it: the behavior itself is what is being checked. Check the result right after the last step.
Steps:
1. Click the memo editor on the home page and type 'apple pie'
2. Click the Save button to save the memo
3. Click the memo editor and type 'banana bread'
4. Click the Save button to save the memo
5. In the sidebar, click the '+' button next to Shortcuts
6. Type 'Banana' in the shortcut title field and type 'content.contains("banana")' in the filter field
7. Click Save in the shortcut dialog
8. Click the search box and type 'apple'
9. Press Enter to run the search
10. Click the 'Banana' item under Shortcuts
The reporter says the correct behavior is that After clicking the 'Banana' shortcut, the search box is empty and the memo 'banana bread' is visible in the list, because only the shortcut filter applies.
